query:
Two members expressed the view that participants should read the game rules before arriving at a session. Which member made the more specific, procedural version of this argument — specifying how and when it should happen?

Options:
A. Tomasz
B. Derek
C. Marcus
D. Raj
context:
[1] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t0 @2026-03-02T19:03:00) Good. In my experience, we should decide the game before the night so people can read the rules. Nothing worse than spending the first hour on a rules explanation.
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t0 @2026-03-02T19:05:00) Seconded. If we're playing something new, whoever owns it should send the rulebook link by Wednesday. Cuts setup time by at least 30 minutes.
[3] (about=Derek, episodic, t0 @2026-03-02T19:04:00) agree. read the rules people
[4] (about=Marcus, episodic, t8 @2026-03-23T19:20:00) Good. Pre-reading counts.
[5] (about=Derek, episodic, t4 @2026-03-09T19:01:00) read it. lets go
[6] (about=Priya, episodic, t3 @2026-03-09T19:00:00) ok we're live at Raj's!! 🎉 rulebooks were sent out Wednesday like Marcus asked, everyone had a chance to look? honestly the Dune theme is doing a lot of heavy lifting for me already
[7] (about=Marcus, episodic, t4 @2026-03-09T19:14:00) We should do the rules rundown for Felix since he hasn't played. Lena, you mentioned the intrigue deck. Want to walk him through that interaction?
[8] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t0 @2026-03-02T19:11:00) Oath has a learning curve that would eat the whole evening. In my experience, new members need something with a shorter rules overhead first. Perhaps we revisit it when everyone has a baseline.
[9] (about=Nadia, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:08:00) It was the most precise rules environment I have played in. He cites historical precedent for every ambiguous ruling.
[10] (about=Nadia, episodic, t2 @2026-04-06T19:33:00) Agreed up front is the correct qualifier. That is not a violation of the rulebook. It is a pre-session variant declaration.
[11] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:03:00) The rule is bring a game or bring food. Both is ideal. Enforcement is just social pressure.
[12] (about=Marcus, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:03:00) It was legal. It was also the correct play given the board state. I would have done the same.
[13] (about=Raj, episodic, t12 @2026-04-13T19:09:00) That tracks. Those two are the most rules-precise people in the group, to be fair 😄
[14] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t1 @2026-03-06T19:32:00) I would normally say no to house rules on principle. But after that session two months ago where the new player left mid-game because the worker placement felt punishing, I think one quality-of-life adjustment for new members is reasonable. Agreed up front.
[15] (about=Marcus, episodic, t10 @2026-03-30T19:53:00) That's actually a reasonable heuristic in a four-player game. Contrarian positioning has value.
[16] (about=Priya, episodic, t10 @2026-03-30T19:45:00) ok post-game debrief time!! Marcus you were incredible at those canal-phase canal placements, how did you know to block the Dudley connection so early?
[17] (about=Lena, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:24:00) Priya you mentioned a relational disclosure earlier that I wanted to follow up on tbh. you and Derek seem to have different vibes about the session energy. like i've noticed he tends to go quiet when cooperative options are even mentioned?
[18] (about=Lena, episodic, t8 @2026-03-23T19:05:00) so basically what Tomasz did was smart pedagogy tbh, scaffolding the experience rather than throwing you in the deep end, the evidence suggests that's actually what determines whether new players stick around
[19] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t2 @2026-04-06T19:01:00) Pierogi are on the stove. Game is Viticulture. In my experience it is a good socialiser since turns are long enough for conversation but short enough to stay engaged.
[20] (about=Nadia, episodic, t6 @2026-03-16T19:02:00) Correct. The intrigue card played was legal. I reviewed it.
[21] (about=Marcus, core, t0 @2026-03-02T19:00:00) Keeps a spreadsheet tracking game statistics, including win/loss records.
[22] (about=GROUP, said_by=Marcus, group-interaction, t0 @2026-03-02T19:00:00) If playing a new game, owner must send rulebook link by Wednesday to cut setup time.
[23] (about=Nadia, core, t2 @2026-04-06T19:00:00) Agrees that agreeing up front is the correct qualifier for house rules, viewing it as a pre-session variant declaration rather than a rulebook violation.
[24] (about=Nadia, core, t12 @2026-04-13T19:01:00) Played a four-session wargame campaign with Tomasz over six weeks last April, describing it as the most precise rules environment she has played in.
[25] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Bring-something rule for marathon: bring a game or food, both ideal; enforcement via social pressure.
[26] (about=Tomasz, core, t0 @2026-03-02T19:00:00) Prefers games with shorter rules overhead for new members; suggests revisiting Oath later when everyone has baseline.
[27] (about=Tomasz, core, t1 @2026-03-06T19:32:00) Normally opposes house rules on principle, but supports one quality-of-life adjustment for new members after a session two months ago where a new player left mid-game due to punishing worker placement.
